sonnet.problem: Both wrong answers are parts of the right answer. The sun and the moon are in the heavens, and the seas and the dry land are on the earth. A baker could argue they are right, since God did make them.
sonnet.rule: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

sonnet.problem: This re-asks a fact the baker already saw in Stop 1. Cards 11 and 13 said the city has been delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans, and the card 14 question repeated it. Handing the city over to the Chaldeans is both the right answer here and an earlier card's content, so the question tests nothing new.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.
